About

What is the Sustainable Olympiad?

What it is

An Olympic format to teach environmental issues

The Sustainable Olympiad uses an Olympic competition format to teach environmental issues. Students test their knowledge about sustainability and the environment, solve challenges with creativity, and earn certificates that open doors to future opportunities.

  • Test knowledge

    About sustainability and the environment.

  • Solve challenges

    With creativity.

  • Earn certificates

    That open doors to future opportunities.

Who created it

A PORTO talks project

PORTO talks logo

The Sustainable Olympiad was created by the PORTO talks project:

“The world as seen by the students”

SDG 4

Quality Education

  • Inclusive, equitable and quality education
  • Improving access to education
  • Reaching people in vulnerable situations
See our objectives

Objectives

What the Olympiad sets out to do

Six objectives guide the Sustainable Olympiad.

  • Increase environmental knowledge among students

  • Improve science education and student engagement

  • Encourage genuine interest in sustainability

  • Identify and develop new talents

  • Promote sustainability and environmental skills

  • Create opportunities through certificates

How it works

Four levels, three phases

Students compete in the level that matches their school year and go through three phases.

Every level goes through the same three phases to complete the competition.

Why it matters

Education is the key to sustainable solutions

The problem

Communities with limited access to education face more environmental problems. Without good education and training, people lack the skills needed to develop sustainable techniques.

What studies show · World Bank and UNESCO
  • Low access to education makes it harder to adapt and to implement sustainable practices.
  • Education provides the knowledge and skills that lead to sustainable solutions.

Benefits

Benefits of education for sustainability

  • Promotes sustainability
  • Improves abilities
  • Sustainability requires cooperation
  • Supports environmental change
  • Protects biodiversity
  • Increases productivity
  • Reduces environmental damage
  • Promotes sustainable techniques

Why olympiads?

Scientific olympiads improve science education, increase student engagement and help discover new talents.

FAQ

Frequently asked questions

Who can participate?

Students from 5th grade to the 3rd year of High School, in four levels:

  • Level 1: 5th and 6th grade
  • Level 2: 7th and 8th grade
  • Level 3: 9th grade and 1st year of High School
  • Level 4: 2nd and 3rd year of High School
How many phases are there?

Three phases, in order:

  • Phase 1 – Test: questions about sustainability and the environment.
  • Phase 2 – Riddle: solve an environmental riddle using knowledge and creativity.
  • Phase 3 – Final Test: a final test to complete the competition.
What topics are covered?

Recycling, Water, Energy, Climate change, Biodiversity and sustainable practices.

Do participants get a certificate?

Yes. Every participant receives a certificate that can be used for future opportunities.
